docs.title: Vexy PDF Werk
docs.text:
Vexy PDF Werk (VPW) is a Python package and a command-line tool, vpw, that takes one PDF file and produces up to four outputs from it:

Format key Output Made by pdfa <stem>_enhanced.pdf, an optimised copy of the PDF, OCR'd to PDF/A-2 when OCR runs ocrmypdf and qpdf markdown One Markdown file per page (or one combined file), each with YAML front matter PyPDF, or Marker, Docling or MarkItDown when installed epub <stem>.epub, one chapter per Markdown page ebooklib yaml metadata.yaml with file, PDF and content facts PyYAML

docs.title: How a run works
docs.text:
You give vpw process a PDF. VPW checks that the file exists, ends in .pdf, is not empty, opens with pikepdf, and has at least one page. It then runs the steps for the formats you asked for, in this order:

  1. pdfa: OCR the file with ocrmypdf if needed, then rewrite it with qpdf --linearize.
  2. Read the PDF's page count, title, author and creation date.
  3. markdown: extract text page by page and write Markdown files.
  4. epub: build an ePub from the Markdown pages.
  5. yaml: write metadata.yaml.

A failed step does not stop later steps. As its last line of output, the command prints 0 if at least one format was produced and 1 otherwise. See Command line for how this relates to the shell exit status.

docs.title: A short example
docs.text:
vpw process report.pdf --formats markdown,yaml

For a three-page report.pdf, this writes to ./output/report/:

output/report/
├── 0--first-meaningful-line-of-page-one.md
├── 1--first-meaningful-line-of-page-two.md
├── 2--first-meaningful-line-of-page-three.md
└── metadata.yaml

docs.title: Project status
docs.text:
VPW is in beta (Development Status :: 4 - Beta). The AI options in the configuration are placeholders and do not change the output yet. See Configuration.

VPW is released under the MIT license. Source code: github.com/vexyart/vexy-pdf-werk.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: VPW is a single pipeline. The CLI checks the input, then calls one processor per output format, in a fixed order, inside one asyncio event loop. External tools run as subprocesses, and the synchronous PDF libraries run in a thread pool.

docs.title: Data flow
docs.text:
┌───────────────────────┐
 report.pdf ───▶  │ validate_pdf_file()   │  pikepdf: exists, .pdf, non-empty, pages > 0
                  └──────────┬────────────┘
                             │
          ┌──────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────┐
          ▼                  ▼                                    │
  PDFProcessor        PDFProcessor.analyze_pdf()                  │
  .create_better_pdf()  → PDFInfo (pages, title, author, ...)     │
   ocrmypdf (optional)       │                                    │
   qpdf --linearize          ▼                                    │
   → <stem>_enhanced.pdf  MarkdownGenerator.generate_markdown()   │
                            BasicConverter | MarkerConverter |    │
                            DoclingConverter | MarkItDownConverter│
                            → MarkdownResult + N--slug.md files   │
                             │                                    │
                             ▼                                    ▼
                       EpubCreator.create_epub()        MetadataExtractor
                         → <stem>.epub                    → metadata.yaml

Each step returns a result object with a success flag instead of raising, so the CLI can report a failed step and go on with the next one.

docs.title: Modules
docs.text: Module Main names Role vexy_pdf_werk.cli VexyPDFWerk, main Fire CLI: process, config, version. Runs the pipeline and prints progress with Rich. vexy_pdf_werk.config VPWConfig, ProcessingConfig, ConversionConfig, AIConfig, OutputConfig, load_config Pydantic settings models, TOML loading and saving, platformdirs paths. vexy_pdf_werk.core.pdf_processor PDFProcessor, PDFInfo, ProcessingResult PDF analysis with pikepdf; OCR with ocrmypdf; final rewrite with qpdf. vexy_pdf_werk.core.markdown_converter MarkdownGenerator, MarkdownConverter, BasicConverter, MarkerConverter, DoclingConverter, MarkItDownConverter, MarkdownResult, MarkdownPage Backend selection, text extraction, page splitting, Markdown file writing. vexy_pdf_werk.core.epub_creator EpubCreator, EpubCreationResult ePub assembly with ebooklib. vexy_pdf_werk.core.metadata_extractor MetadataExtractor, DocumentMetadata Builds and writes metadata.yaml. vexy_pdf_werk.core.qdf_processor QDFProcessor Converts a page to qpdf's QDF/JSON form and applies text diffs. Used only by the experimental AI structure step. vexy_pdf_werk.integrations.ai_services AIServiceFactory, ClaudeCLIService, GeminiCLIService Wrappers that call the claude and gemini command-line tools. Experimental. vexy_pdf_werk.utils.validation validate_pdf_file, validate_output_directory, validate_formats Input checks shared by the CLI and processors. vexy_pdf_werk.utils.slug_utils generate_page_slug, sanitize_file_slug File-name slugs from page text (unicode-slugify, pathvalidate). vexy_pdf_werk.utils.file_utils find_tool_path, ensure_directory, safe_copy_file, generate_output_filename, cleanup_temp_files Small file-system helpers. vexy_pdf_werk.vexy_pdf_werk Config, process_data, main Legacy placeholder API, re-exported from the package root. vexy_pdf_werk.simple_cli, vexy_pdf_werk.simple_config SimplePDFConverter, SimpleConfig A reduced CLI and config. They have no installed command.

docs.title: Backend selection
docs.text:
MarkdownGenerator._create_converter() maps conversion.markdown_backend to a converter class. For "auto", it builds each optional converter in turn and keeps the first whose __init__ managed to import its library. Each optional converter also catches errors during conversion and returns the BasicConverter result instead. This makes the Markdown step hard to break, but it also means a misconfigured backend fails silently. Run with --verbose and look at the number and shape of the pages to see which backend ran.

The optional backends return one document-wide Markdown string. VPW splits it at headings to keep the "one MarkdownPage per file" interface. Only BasicConverter maps files to PDF pages one to one.

docs.title: Concurrency
docs.text:
• ocrmypdf and qpdf run through asyncio.create_subprocess_exec, and their stderr becomes the error message on failure.
  • PyPDF reading, Marker, Docling and MarkItDown run in a ThreadPoolExecutor through loop.run_in_executor.
  • Markdown files are written with aiofiles.

The steps themselves run one after another, because each later step needs the result of an earlier one.

docs.title: External tools
docs.text:
Tool Found by Used for ocrmypdf PATH lookup when PDFProcessor is created; missing tool raises RuntimeError OCR and PDF/A-2 output qpdf PATH lookup when PDFProcessor is created; missing tool raises RuntimeError Linearisation; QDF/JSON in the AI step tesseract, Ghostscript By ocrmypdf OCR engine; PDF/A rendering claude, gemini Called by name in the AI step Experimental AI services

Because PDFProcessor is created at the start of every vpw process run, ocrmypdf and qpdf must be installed even when you request no pdfa output.

docs.title: Logging
docs.text: VPW logs with loguru to stderr. Loguru's default sink logs at the DEBUG level, so every run prints debug messages. --verbose re-adds the sink at the same level and makes the CLI print a traceback when a run fails. The legacy module vexy_pdf_werk.vexy_pdf_werk also configures the standard logging module at INFO on import, so some libraries, such as pikepdf, print INFO lines.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
The vpw command has three subcommands: process, config and version. It is built with Python Fire, so each flag can be written with an underscore or a hyphen (--output_dir or --output-dir) and has a one-letter short form.

You can also start the CLI as a module:

python -m vexy_pdf_werk process document.pdf

To see help for a subcommand, run it with --help:

vpw process --help

docs.title: vpw process
docs.text:
Converts one PDF file into the requested formats.

vpw process PDF_PATH [--output_dir DIR] [--formats LIST] [--verbose] [--config_file FILE]
Argument Short Default Meaning PDF_PATH (required) Path to the input PDF file. --output_dir -o ./output/<stem> Folder for all outputs. Created if missing. --formats -f pdfa,markdown,epub,yaml Comma-separated list of formats to produce. --verbose -v off Print a Python traceback when the run fails. Debug logging is on in every run. --config_file -c the user config file Path to a config.toml to use instead of the default one.

docs.title: Formats
docs.text:
--formats accepts these keys, in any order and any letter case:

  • pdfa: write <stem>_enhanced.pdf.
  • markdown: write one Markdown file per page.
  • epub: write <stem>.epub. Markdown is converted even if you did not ask for it.
  • yaml: write metadata.yaml.

Duplicate keys are ignored. An unknown key stops the run before any work starts:

Error: Invalid output format: html. Available formats: pdfa, markdown, epub, yaml

The steps always run in the order pdfa, markdown, epub, yaml, whatever order you list them in.

docs.title: What process checks first
docs.text:
Before the pipeline starts, vpw process rejects the input with Error: ... and the result 1 when:

  • the file does not exist;
  • the path is a folder;
  • the name does not end in .pdf;
  • the file is empty;
  • pikepdf cannot open it, it is password-protected, or it has no pages;
  • --output_dir exists and is a file.

docs.title: Result and exit status
docs.text:
vpw process returns a result code, and Fire prints it as the last line of output:

Printed result Meaning 0 At least one requested format was produced. 1 Invalid input, invalid format list, missing ocrmypdf or qpdf, or no format was produced.

The shell exit status does not follow the result

In the current version, the process exits with status 0 even when the printed result is 1. The exit status is non-zero only when an unexpected error reaches the top level (status 1, for example an invalid config.toml) or when Fire rejects the command line (status 2). In scripts, check the last output line or the files in the output folder instead of $?.

A step that fails prints ✗ and a reason, and the remaining steps still run. For example, if the pdfa step fails, VPW prints Continuing with original PDF for other formats... and goes on to Markdown.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Convert to Markdown only, into a chosen folder:

vpw process paper.pdf --formats markdown --output_dir ./paper-md

Use a project-specific configuration file:

vpw process scan.pdf -c ./scan-config.toml

Get a traceback while you track down a failure:

vpw process broken.pdf --verbose

Convert every PDF in a folder (shell loop):

for f in pdfs/*.pdf; do
  vpw process "$f" --formats markdown,yaml
done

Each file gets its own ./output/<stem>/ folder.

docs.title: vpw config
docs.text:
Creates or shows the user configuration file.

vpw config [--init] [--show]
Flag Short Meaning --init -i Write a config.toml with all default values, unless the file already exists. --show -s Print the path of the config file and the main settings VPW will use.

With neither flag, vpw config prints Use --show to display config or --init to create default config.

vpw config --show always reads the default user file. It has no --config_file flag. If the file does not exist, it shows the built-in defaults.

vpw config --init
vpw config --show

Configuration loaded from: /Users/you/Library/Application Support/vexy-pdf-werk/config.toml

Current Configuration:
Processing:
  OCR Language: eng
  PDF Quality: high
  Force OCR: False
Conversion:
  Markdown Backend: auto
  Paginate Markdown: True
  Include Images: True
AI:
  Enabled: False
  Provider: claude
  Correction Enabled: False
Output:
  Formats: pdfa, markdown, epub, yaml
  Output Directory: ./output
  Preserve Original: True

The file location depends on the operating system. See Configuration.

docs.title: vpw version
docs.text:
Prints the installed version:

vpw version

Vexy PDF Werk version 1.2.1

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: VPW reads its settings from a TOML file and a few environment variables. Settings it does not find keep their built-in defaults, so you need a file only to change something.

docs.title: Where the file lives
docs.text:
VPW uses the user configuration folder that the platformdirs package returns for the application name vexy-pdf-werk:

System Default path macOS ~/Library/Application Support/vexy-pdf-werk/config.toml Linux ~/.config/vexy-pdf-werk/config.toml (or $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/vexy-pdf-werk/config.toml) Windows config.toml in the platformdirs user config folder under %LOCALAPPDATA%

To print the exact path on your machine, run vpw config --show. The first line shows it.

To use a different file for one run, pass it to vpw process:

vpw process document.pdf --config_file ./my-config.toml

If the file you name does not exist, VPW uses the defaults without a warning.

docs.title: Create the file
docs.text:
1. Write a file with every default value:

    vpw config --init

    VPW prints Created default configuration at: and the path. If a file is already there, VPW leaves it unchanged.

  2. Open the file in a text editor and change the values you need.

  3. Check the result:

    vpw config --show

docs.title: Default file
docs.text:
vpw config --init writes this:

[processing]
ocr_language = "eng"
pdf_quality = "high"
force_ocr = false
deskew = true
rotate_pages = true

[conversion]
markdown_backend = "auto"
paginate_markdown = true
include_images = true
extract_tables = true

[ai]
enabled = false
provider = "claude"
correction_enabled = false
enhancement_enabled = false
structure_enhancement_enabled = false
max_tokens = 4000

[output]
formats = [ "pdfa", "markdown", "epub", "yaml",]
preserve_original = true
output_directory = "./output"
filename_template = "{stem}_{format}.{ext}"

The file is validated with Pydantic models. A value of the wrong type, such as force_ocr = "maybe", stops the run with an error. Unknown keys are ignored.

docs.title: [processing] section
docs.text:
These settings control the pdfa step. They are passed to ocrmypdf when OCR runs.

Key Default Effect ocr_language "eng" Passed as ocrmypdf --language. Use Tesseract language codes, for example "deu" or "eng+fra". The language data must be installed. pdf_quality "high" "high" passes --optimize 1 to ocrmypdf. Any other value passes --optimize 0. force_ocr false true runs OCR on every page, replacing any existing text layer (ocrmypdf --force-ocr). deskew true Adds ocrmypdf --deskew. rotate_pages true Adds ocrmypdf --rotate-pages.

OCR runs only when VPW classes the PDF as scanned or when force_ocr = true. See Output formats.

docs.title: [conversion] section
docs.text:
Key Default Effect markdown_backend "auto" Which converter makes the Markdown. One of "auto", "marker", "docling", "markitdown", "basic". paginate_markdown true true writes one file per page. false writes one file, <stem>.md. include_images true Shown by vpw config --show. No converter reads it yet. extract_tables true Not read by any converter yet.

How markdown_backend is resolved:

  • "auto" tries marker, then docling, then markitdown, and uses the first one whose package imports. If none imports, it uses basic.
  • "marker", "docling" or "markitdown" use that backend. If its package is missing, or the conversion raises an error, VPW falls back to basic without a message.
  • "basic" always uses PyPDF.
  • Any other value uses basic.

docs.title: [ai] section
docs.text:
The AI settings are experimental. In the current version they do not change any output:

  • correction_enabled = true (with enabled = true) copies the PDF unchanged and logs AI enhancement not yet implemented, skipping.
  • structure_enhancement_enabled = true (with enabled = true) sends each page's text to the claude or gemini command-line tool, if one is installed, but writes the original pages back.
  • enhancement_enabled and max_tokens are not used by the pipeline.

provider accepts "claude" or "gemini". Leave enabled = false unless you are working on this feature.

docs.title: [output] section
docs.text: vpw process does not read this section. Its formats and output folder come from the --formats and --output_dir flags and their defaults. vpw config --show prints formats, output_directory and preserve_original from here. filename_template is not used.

docs.title: Top-level keys
docs.text: Key Default Effect tesseract_path not set Stored on the processor, but not passed to ocrmypdf, which finds Tesseract on PATH. qpdf_path not set Not used. VPW finds qpdf on PATH. pandoc_path not set Not used.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Variable Effect TESSERACT_PATH Sets tesseract_path. Same limits as the key above. QPDF_PATH Sets qpdf_path, which is not used. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GOOGLE_AI_API_KEY, DATALAB_API_KEY Read into the [ai] section, but the AI settings model has no field for them, so they are discarded.

API key variables replace the [ai] section

When any of ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GOOGLE_AI_API_KEY or DATALAB_API_KEY is set, VPW builds a new [ai] section from the variables and drops the one in your file. Your [ai] values then fall back to defaults. This matters only if you use the experimental AI settings.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: This page covers the development setup, tests, the documentation build and the release process.

docs.title: Set up a development environment
docs.text:
Prerequisites: Git, uv, and ocrmypdf and qpdf on your PATH for end-to-end runs.

  1. Clone the repository:

    git clone https://github.com/vexyart/vexy-pdf-werk
cd vexy-pdf-werk

  2. Install the package in editable mode with the test and development extras:

    uv sync --extra test --extra dev

  3. Check the command:

    uv run vpw version

docs.title: Repository layout
docs.text: Path Contents src/vexy_pdf_werk/ Package source. See Architecture. tests/ pytest tests, one file per module (test_cli.py, test_markdown_converter.py, ...). examples/ Sample PDFs in examples/data/, plus Python and shell example scripts. src_docs/ Documentation source (src_docs/md/), mkdocs.yml and build.sh. docs/ Built documentation site, served by GitHub Pages. Do not edit by hand. build.sh, publish.sh Build and release scripts.

docs.title: Run the tests
docs.text:
Run the whole suite:

uv run --extra test pytest

Run one file or one test:

uv run --extra test pytest tests/test_markdown_converter.py
uv run --extra test pytest tests/test_cli.py -k config

The pytest settings in pyproject.toml add -v --durations=10 and set asyncio_mode = "auto", so async def tests run without a decorator.

docs.title: Lint and type-check
docs.text:
uvx ruff check src tests
uvx ruff format --respect-gitignore src tests
uvx mypy src/vexy_pdf_werk

The push.yml workflow runs ruff check and ruff format --check, then the tests on Python 3.10, 3.11 and 3.12, then builds the wheel and sdist.

docs.title: Build the documentation
docs.text:
The site is built with ProperDocs and the MaterialX theme from the Markdown files in src_docs/md/.

  1. Edit or add pages in src_docs/md/. Add new pages to the nav list in src_docs/mkdocs.yml.

  2. Preview the site:

    src_docs/build.sh serve

    Open http://127.0.0.1:8000 in a browser. The page reloads when you save a file.

  3. Build the site into docs/:

    src_docs/build.sh

    The build runs in strict mode, so a warning, such as a link to a missing page, stops it.

You do not need to commit docs/ yourself. The docs.yml workflow rebuilds docs/ and commits it on every push to main that changes src_docs/.

docs.title: Build the package
docs.text:
./build.sh package

This deletes dist/, runs uv build, and checks the result with twine check. ./build.sh with no argument also builds the documentation, and ./build.sh docs builds only the documentation.

The version comes from the latest Git tag through hatch-vcs. Between tags, the built version is a development version such as 1.2.2.dev3.

docs.title: Release a new version
docs.text:
Releases are made from a clean main branch with publish.sh.

Prerequisites: a PyPI token in UV_PUBLISH_TOKEN (or another credential that uv publish accepts), and push access to the repository.

  1. Run:

    ./publish.sh

  2. The script runs uvx gitnextver, which commits pending changes, creates the next vX.Y.Z tag and pushes it.

  3. If HEAD now carries a vX.Y.Z tag, the script builds the package with ./build.sh package and uploads dist/* with uv publish. If there was nothing to commit and no tag was made, it stops with an error.

Pushing the tag also starts the release.yml workflow. It builds the package again, uploads it to PyPI (skipping files that publish.sh already uploaded), and creates a GitHub release with the built files attached.

docs.title: Pull requests
docs.text:
1. Create a branch from main.
  2. Make the change and add or update tests for it.
  3. Run the tests and ruff.
  4. If the change affects behaviour, update the pages in src_docs/md/ and CHANGELOG.md.
  5. Open a pull request against main.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: VPW needs three things: the Python package, two external command-line tools that every run uses, and, optionally, one or more advanced Markdown converters.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python 3.10 or newer.
  • ocrmypdf on your PATH. Every vpw process run needs it, even when you ask only for markdown or yaml, because VPW locates the tool when it starts the pipeline.
  • qpdf on your PATH. Every run needs it for the same reason.
  • tesseract, with the language data for the documents you OCR. ocrmypdf calls it.
  • Ghostscript (gs). ocrmypdf uses it to write PDF/A output.

The Python dependencies (pikepdf, pypdf, ebooklib, pydantic, fire, rich, loguru and others) install automatically with the package.

docs.title: Install the Python package
docs.text:
1. Install VPW from PyPI:

    uv tool install vexy-pdf-werk

    Or, with pip:

    python -m pip install vexy-pdf-werk

  2. Check that the vpw command works:

    vpw version

    The command prints Vexy PDF Werk version followed by the installed version.

docs.title: Install the external tools
docs.text:
ocrmypdf is a Python application. You can install it with your system package manager or as a uv tool:

uv tool install ocrmypdf

Install the other tools with your system package manager.

macOSUbuntu and DebianWindows 
brew install ocrmypdf qpdf tesseract tesseract-lang ghostscript

sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install ocrmypdf qpdf tesseract-ocr tesseract-ocr-eng ghostscript

choco install qpdf tesseract ghostscript
python -m pip install ocrmypdf

Check that VPW will find them:

ocrmypdf --version
qpdf --version
tesseract --version

Tool paths

VPW looks up ocrmypdf and qpdf on PATH only. The tesseract_path setting and the TESSERACT_PATH environment variable are stored, but ocrmypdf still finds Tesseract on its own. See Configuration.

docs.title: Optional Markdown converters
docs.text:
Without extra packages, VPW extracts text with PyPDF (the basic backend). Three other backends become available when you install their packages into the same environment as VPW:

Backend Package to install Import VPW checks marker marker-pdf marker.converters.pdf.PdfConverter docling docling docling.document_converter.DocumentConverter markitdown markitdown markitdown.MarkItDown

To add a backend to a uv tool install:

uv tool install vexy-pdf-werk --with marker-pdf

To add it to a pip environment:

python -m pip install marker-pdf

No extras for converters

The package defines no [all] or [epub] extra that installs these converters. Install each one by name. ebooklib, which the ePub step needs, is already a core dependency.

With markdown_backend = "auto" (the default), VPW uses the first backend it can import, in this order: marker, docling, markitdown, basic. See Configuration.

docs.title: Install from source
docs.text:
1. Clone the repository:

    git clone https://github.com/vexyart/vexy-pdf-werk
cd vexy-pdf-werk

  2. Create the environment and install the package with its test tools:

    uv sync --extra test

  3. Run the command from the environment:

    uv run vpw version

The version number comes from the latest Git tag. hatch-vcs writes it to src/vexy_pdf_werk/_version.py when the package is built or installed. If that file is missing, vexy_pdf_werk.__version__ falls back to 0.0.0+dev.

docs.title: Output formats
docs.text:
All outputs go into one folder: --output_dir, or ./output/<stem>/ by default. <stem> is the input file name without .pdf. Existing files with the same names are overwritten.

Format key File(s) pdfa <stem>_enhanced.pdf markdown <N>--<slug>.md per page, or <stem>.md epub <stem>.epub yaml metadata.yaml

docs.title: Enhanced PDF (pdfa)
docs.text: The pdfa step writes <stem>_enhanced.pdf. What that file is depends on whether OCR runs.

docs.title: When OCR runs
docs.text:
VPW first inspects up to the first three pages with pikepdf. It counts a page as having text when the page has a /Contents entry, and as having images when its resources contain an image XObject. It classes the document as scanned when it found images and fewer than half of the sampled pages had text.

OCR runs when the document is classed as scanned, or when force_ocr = true in the configuration. Because almost every PDF page has a /Contents entry, the scanned check rarely triggers. For scanned documents, set force_ocr = true.

docs.title: The two paths
docs.text:
1. With OCR: VPW runs ocrmypdf with --output-type pdfa-2, the OCR language, the optimisation level, --deskew and --rotate-pages (if enabled), and --force-ocr or --skip-text. It also passes the PDF's title and author if they are set. The result is PDF/A-2b with a searchable text layer. VPW then runs qpdf --linearize --object-streams=generate on it.
  2. Without OCR: VPW runs only qpdf --linearize --object-streams=generate on the original. The output is a linearised ("fast web view") copy with compressed object streams. It is not converted to PDF/A.

If either tool fails, VPW prints PDF enhancement failed: with the tool's error message and continues with the other formats. The original PDF is never modified.

docs.title: One file per page
docs.text:
With paginate_markdown = true (the default), VPW writes one file per page named <N>--<slug>.md:

  • <N> is the page index, starting at 0. It is zero-padded to the width of the last index: 0–9 for up to 10 pages, 00–99 for up to 100 pages, and so on.
  • <slug> comes from the page text. VPW takes the first line longer than 10 characters, removes the characters #, *, _, [, ], (, ) and the backtick, cuts it to at most 50 characters at a word boundary, and turns it into a lowercase hyphenated slug. A blank page gets empty-page. A slug shorter than 3 characters becomes page-content.

Each file starts with YAML front matter:

---
page: 1
total_pages: 3
title: "Two-Column Document with Lorem Ipsum"
slug: "two-column-document-with-lorem-ipsum"
---

Two-Column Document with Lorem Ipsum
...
  • page is the 1-based page number.
  • total_pages is the number of Markdown pages written.
  • title is the first non-empty line, if it is 6 to 99 characters long and contains a letter. Otherwise the key is left out.
  • slug is the slug used in the file name.

docs.title: One combined file
docs.text: With paginate_markdown = false, VPW writes <stem>.md. It starts with # <stem>, and each page follows under a ## Page <n> heading, with --- between pages. No front matter is written.

docs.title: What the basic backend produces
docs.text:
The basic backend extracts text with PyPDF, page by page, so file 0--… always holds PDF page 1. It then:

  • trims each line and keeps at most two blank lines in a row;
  • collapses runs of three or more spaces to two;
  • turns a line into a ## heading when more than 70 % of its words are upper case or non-alphabetic and the line is under 80 characters, or when it starts with a number followed by a capital letter (1. Introduction, 2 Methods);
  • writes [Page N appears to be empty or contains only images] for a page with no extractable text.

docs.title: What the other backends produce
docs.text: marker, docling and markitdown convert the whole document to one Markdown text. VPW then splits that text at headings (# and ## for Marker, # to ### for Docling and MarkItDown). Each "page" is therefore a section, not a PDF page, and the number of Markdown files can differ from the PDF page count.

docs.title: ePub (epub)
docs.text:
The epub step builds <stem>.epub with ebooklib from the Markdown pages:

  • one chapter per Markdown page, named page_000.xhtml or page_000_<slug>.xhtml;
  • a table of contents with one entry per chapter, plus NCX and navigation files;
  • the language set to en and a random UUID as the identifier.

The book title is the first page's title if there is one, otherwise the PDF's /Title, otherwise the file stem with _ and - replaced by spaces and each word capitalised. The author is the PDF's /Author, or VPW User if it is not set.

The Markdown-to-HTML conversion is simple: lines starting with #, ## or ### become headings, other lines become <p> paragraphs, and blank lines become <br/>. Lists, emphasis, links and tables are not converted.

If the Markdown step failed, VPW prints ePub generation skipped - markdown conversion required.

docs.title: Metadata (yaml)
docs.text:
The yaml step writes metadata.yaml with four groups:

document:
  source_file: multicolumn.pdf
  source_size_bytes: 78657
  processed_at: '2026-10-12T20:39:26.512117+00:00'
  processing_time_seconds: 0.22
pdf_info:
  pages: 3
  has_text: true
  is_scanned: false
  has_images: false
  creation_date: D:20240103093826+01'00'
processing:
  formats_generated:
  - pdfa
  - markdown
  - epub
  markdown_pages: 3
content:
  estimated_word_count: 1061
  first_page_preview: Two-Column Document with Lorem Ipsum Your Name January 3, 2024
    Abstract This is a sample document with two columns ﬁlled
Key Source document.processed_at UTC time when the metadata was written, ISO 8601. document.processing_time_seconds Time from the start of the pipeline to the metadata step. pdf_info.* The pikepdf analysis described above. title, author and creation_date appear only when the PDF sets them. creation_date is the raw PDF date string. processing.formats_generated Formats finished before this step. yaml is never listed. processing.markdown_pages Number of Markdown pages, or 0 if Markdown was not made. content.estimated_word_count Whitespace-separated words longer than one character, skipping words that start with # and ---. 0 without Markdown. content.first_page_preview Up to 200 characters from the first lines of the first page, skipping headings. Left out when there is no Markdown.

docs.title: Python API
docs.text:
The vpw command is a thin layer over a few classes that you can use directly. Most methods are async, so call them from an event loop, for example with asyncio.run().

Top-level names

from vexy_pdf_werk import Config, process_data, main gives you legacy placeholders kept for backward compatibility. process_data() only returns a dictionary that points you to vpw process. Import the classes below from their modules instead.

docs.title: Convert a PDF to Markdown
docs.text:
MarkdownGenerator picks a backend from a ConversionConfig, converts the PDF, and writes the Markdown files.

import asyncio
from pathlib import Path

from vexy_pdf_werk.config import ConversionConfig
from vexy_pdf_werk.core.markdown_converter import MarkdownGenerator


async def main() -> None:
    generator = MarkdownGenerator(ConversionConfig(markdown_backend="basic"))
    result = await generator.generate_markdown(Path("report.pdf"), Path("out"))
    if not result.success:
        raise SystemExit(result.error)
    for page in result.pages:
        print(page.page_number, page.slug, page.title)


asyncio.run(main())

generate_markdown(pdf_path, output_dir) returns a MarkdownResult. When success is True, the files are already written to output_dir.

MarkdownResult field Type Meaning success bool False when the conversion raised an error. pages list[MarkdownPage] Converted pages. Empty on failure. error str or None Error message on failure. total_pages int Number of pages converted. processing_time float Seconds spent converting. MarkdownPage field Type Meaning page_number int 0-based index. content str Markdown text, without front matter. title str or None Title from the first line, if it qualifies. slug str or None Slug used in the file name.

To convert without writing files, call the converter directly:

from vexy_pdf_werk.core.markdown_converter import BasicConverter

result = await BasicConverter(ConversionConfig()).convert_pdf(Path("report.pdf"))

The converter classes are BasicConverter, MarkerConverter, DoclingConverter and MarkItDownConverter. All take a ConversionConfig and implement async convert_pdf(pdf_path) -> MarkdownResult. The three optional ones fall back to BasicConverter when their package is missing.

docs.title: Analyse and enhance a PDF
docs.text:
PDFProcessor needs a full VPWConfig. Creating it raises RuntimeError if ocrmypdf or qpdf is not on PATH.

from vexy_pdf_werk.config import load_config
from vexy_pdf_werk.core.pdf_processor import PDFProcessor


async def enhance() -> None:
    processor = PDFProcessor(load_config())

    info = await processor.analyze_pdf(Path("scan.pdf"))
    print(info.pages, info.has_text, info.is_scanned, info.title)

    result = await processor.create_better_pdf(Path("scan.pdf"), Path("out/scan_enhanced.pdf"))
    print(result.success, result.error)
  • analyze_pdf(pdf_path) returns a PDFInfo with path, pages, has_text, is_scanned, has_images, title, author and creation_date. It raises RuntimeError if the file cannot be analysed.
  • create_better_pdf(pdf_path, output_path, progress=None, task_id=None) returns a ProcessingResult with success, output_path, pdf_info, error and processing_time. It does not raise on tool failures; check success. The optional progress and task_id are a Rich Progress and task ID whose description it updates.

docs.title: Build an ePub
docs.text:
from vexy_pdf_werk.core.epub_creator import EpubCreator

creator = EpubCreator(book_title="Annual report", author="Jane Doe")
epub_result = await creator.create_epub(result, Path("out/report.epub"), Path("report.pdf"))

create_epub(markdown_result, output_path, source_pdf_path=None) returns an EpubCreationResult with success, output_path, error and processing_time.

For non-async code, create_epub_from_markdown(markdown_result, output_path, book_title=None, author=None, source_pdf_path=None) in the same module wraps the call in asyncio.run().

docs.title: Write metadata
docs.text:
MetadataExtractor is synchronous:

from vexy_pdf_werk.core.metadata_extractor import MetadataExtractor

extractor = MetadataExtractor()
metadata = extractor.extract_metadata(
    Path("report.pdf"), info, markdown_result=result, formats_generated=["markdown"], processing_time=1.5
)
extractor.save_metadata_yaml(metadata, Path("out/metadata.yaml"))

extract_metadata() returns a DocumentMetadata dataclass. save_metadata_yaml() writes it in the grouped layout shown in Output formats.

docs.title: Load and save configuration
docs.text:
Functions in vexy_pdf_werk.config:

Function Purpose load_config(config_file=None) Read the TOML file (default: the user file) and environment variables into a VPWConfig. save_config(config, config_file=None) Write a VPWConfig as TOML, creating the folder. create_default_config() Write the defaults to the user file if it does not exist, and return them. get_config_dir() / get_config_file() Return the user config folder or file path.

VPWConfig has the sections processing (ProcessingConfig), conversion (ConversionConfig), ai (AIConfig) and output (OutputConfig). They are Pydantic models, so you can build them in code:

from vexy_pdf_werk.config import ProcessingConfig, VPWConfig

config = VPWConfig(processing=ProcessingConfig(force_ocr=True, ocr_language="deu"))

docs.title: Utility functions
docs.text: Function Module Purpose validate_pdf_file(path) vexy_pdf_werk.utils.validation Raise FileNotFoundError or ValueError if the path is not a readable, non-empty PDF with pages. validate_formats(formats) vexy_pdf_werk.utils.validation Lowercase, de-duplicate and check a list of format keys. generate_page_slug(content, max_length=50) vexy_pdf_werk.utils.slug_utils Make a file-name slug from page text. find_tool_path(tool_name) vexy_pdf_werk.utils.file_utils Return the full path of a command on PATH, or None.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text: This page converts one PDF into all four formats and shows what each output file contains. The example uses multicolumn.pdf, a three-page two-column document from the repository's examples/data/ folder. Any text-based PDF works the same way.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• VPW is installed and vpw version works. See Installation.
  • ocrmypdf and qpdf are on your PATH.

docs.title: Convert a PDF
docs.text:
1. Run vpw process on the file:

    vpw process multicolumn.pdf

    VPW prints the input path, the output directory and the requested formats, then shows one progress line per step. The run ends with a summary:

    Processing completed in 0.3s
Formats created: pdfa, markdown, epub, yaml
Output directory: output/multicolumn
0

    The final 0 is the command's result: at least one format was produced. See Command line.

  2. List the output directory:

    ls output/multicolumn

    0--two-column-document-with-lorem-ipsum.md
1--lacus-vel-est-curabitur-consectetuer.md
2--table-1-eu-countries-information.md
metadata.yaml
multicolumn.epub
multicolumn_enhanced.pdf

When you give no --output_dir, VPW writes to ./output/<stem>/, where <stem> is the PDF file name without .pdf. It creates the directory if needed.

docs.title: Read the results
docs.text:
Each Markdown file holds one page. The number before -- is the page index, starting at 0. The text after -- is a slug made from the first line on the page that is longer than 10 characters. The file starts with YAML front matter:

---
page: 1
total_pages: 3
title: "Two-Column Document with Lorem Ipsum"
slug: "two-column-document-with-lorem-ipsum"
---

Two-Column Document with Lorem Ipsum
Your Name
January 3, 2024
Abstract
...

metadata.yaml describes the source file and the run:

document:
  source_file: multicolumn.pdf
  source_size_bytes: 78657
  processed_at: '2026-10-12T20:39:26.512117+00:00'
  processing_time_seconds: 0.22
pdf_info:
  pages: 3
  has_text: true
  is_scanned: false
  has_images: false
  creation_date: D:20240103093826+01'00'
processing:
  formats_generated:
  - pdfa
  - markdown
  - epub
  markdown_pages: 3
content:
  estimated_word_count: 1061
  first_page_preview: Two-Column Document with Lorem Ipsum Your Name January 3, 2024
    Abstract This is a sample document with two columns ﬁlled

formats_generated lists the formats finished before the metadata step, so it never includes yaml itself.

multicolumn.epub has one chapter per Markdown file. multicolumn_enhanced.pdf is the processed PDF. For this file no OCR ran, so it is a linearised copy of the original. See Output formats for when VPW applies OCR and PDF/A.

docs.title: Choose formats and a folder
docs.text:
Ask for a subset of formats with --formats and a different folder with --output_dir:

vpw process multicolumn.pdf --formats markdown,yaml --output_dir ./notes

This writes only the three Markdown files and metadata.yaml into ./notes.

If you ask for epub without markdown, VPW still converts to Markdown, because the ePub is built from it. The Markdown files are written to the output folder in that case too.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• See every flag in Command line.
  • Switch the Markdown backend or OCR language in Configuration.
  • Call the converters from Python in Python API.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
VPW logs every step at the DEBUG level to standard error, so most runs already show where a problem started. Add --verbose to also print a Python traceback when the run fails:

vpw process document.pdf --verbose

docs.title: Required tool 'ocrmypdf' not found in PATH
docs.text:
Initialization Failed - RuntimeError:
  Required tool 'ocrmypdf' not found in PATH. Please install it.

Cause: VPW checks for ocrmypdf and qpdf at the start of every run, even when you ask only for markdown or yaml.

Fix:

  1. Install ocrmypdf, for example with uv tool install ocrmypdf or brew install ocrmypdf.
  2. Check that the shell finds it: ocrmypdf --version.
  3. Run vpw process again.

The same message with 'qpdf' means qpdf is missing. Install it with your system package manager. See Installation.

docs.title: Error: File must have .pdf extension
docs.text:
VPW checks the file name, not the content. Rename the file so it ends in .pdf (any letter case).

Other messages from the input check:

Message Meaning PDF file not found: ... The path does not exist. Check the spelling and the current folder. Path is not a file: ... The path is a folder. Pass one PDF file. For many files, use a shell loop. PDF file is empty: ... The file has 0 bytes. PDF file is password protected: ... Remove the password first, for example with qpdf --decrypt --password=... in.pdf out.pdf. PDF structure error: ... pikepdf could not parse the file. Try qpdf --check on it, or repair it with qpdf in.pdf out.pdf. PDF file has no pages: ... The PDF opens but contains no pages.

docs.title: The enhanced PDF has no text layer
docs.text:
Cause: VPW ran OCR only if it classed the PDF as scanned, and that check rarely triggers. Without OCR, <stem>_enhanced.pdf is just a linearised copy.

Fix: set force_ocr = true in the [processing] section of your config file, or in a separate file you pass with --config_file:

[processing]
force_ocr = true
ocr_language = "eng"

Then run vpw process scan.pdf --formats pdfa.

docs.title: PDF enhancement failed: OCR processing failed: ...
docs.text:
The text after the colon is ocrmypdf's own error output. Common causes:

  • The language data for ocr_language is not installed. Install the Tesseract language pack, for example tesseract-ocr-deu on Debian or tesseract-lang on macOS.
  • Ghostscript is missing, so PDF/A output cannot be written. Install ghostscript.

The other formats are still produced after this error.

docs.title: The Markdown pages are empty or say "appears to be empty"
docs.text:
[Page 3 appears to be empty or contains only images]

Cause: the basic backend reads only the existing text layer. A scanned page has none.

Fix: either install an optional backend that does its own layout and OCR analysis, such as marker-pdf or docling, or create a text layer first:

  1. Run vpw process scan.pdf --formats pdfa with force_ocr = true.
  2. Run vpw process output/scan/scan_enhanced.pdf --formats markdown.

docs.title: My chosen backend was not used
docs.text:
If markdown_backend is "marker", "docling" or "markitdown" and the package is not importable, or the conversion raises an error, VPW uses basic without a message. Check that the package is installed in the same environment as VPW:

python -c "import marker; import docling; import markitdown"

For a uv tool install, reinstall with the package: uv tool install vexy-pdf-werk --with marker-pdf.

docs.title: Invalid output format
docs.text:
Error: Invalid output format: md. Available formats: pdfa, markdown, epub, yaml

Use the exact keys pdfa, markdown, epub and yaml, separated by commas without spaces, or quote the list: --formats "markdown, yaml".

docs.title: Configuration Error or Unexpected Error - ValidationError
docs.text:
A value in config.toml has the wrong type, or the file is not valid TOML.

  1. Run vpw config --show to see the path of the file.
  2. Fix the value, or move the file away and run vpw config --init to write a fresh default file.

docs.title: The banner shows <bound method ...>
docs.text: vpw process prints a line like Vexy PDF Werk v<bound method VexyPDFWerk.version ...> instead of the version number. This is a known cosmetic bug in the banner and does not affect processing. Use vpw version to see the version.

docs.title: Reporting a bug
docs.text: Open an issue at github.com/vexyart/vexy-pdf-werk/issues. Include the command you ran, the output of vpw version, and the full output of the run with --verbose.
